name: Casco Historico
tagline: Golden-stone heart around the Plaza Mayor
description: The UNESCO historic core, wrapped around the baroque Plaza Mayor and paved in glowing Villamayor sandstone. Monuments, tapas bars, and cafes sit at every turn, and everything is walkable. It is the postcard Salamanca and the liveliest place to be based.
bestFor: Culture lovers wanting monuments, cafes, and nightlife on their doorstep
pros: Best tapas and cafe options in the city

name: Barrio Universitario
tagline: Bookish quarter by the ancient university
description: The student heartland around the University of Salamanca, home to the famous frog facade and centuries of scholarship. Streets buzz with young energy, cheap eateries, and language schools. Handsome, historic, and sociable, it blends seamlessly into the neighbouring old town.
bestFor: Students, Spanish learners, and sociable nomads seeking a young crowd

name: Van Dyck / San Bernardo
tagline: Local tapas streets north of centre
description: A residential, everyday district north of the old town, famous among locals for its dense run of tapas bars along Calle Van Dyck. Less touristy and more affordable than the centre, it offers real neighbourhood life while staying an easy walk from the monuments.
bestFor: Value seekers wanting authentic tapas and everyday local living
pros: Lower rents than the historic core

name: Garrido
tagline: Affordable residential district for longer stays
description: A large, practical residential neighbourhood on the city's western side, popular with families and students for its lower rents. It offers supermarkets, parks, and everyday services rather than sights, with buses and a walk linking you back to the centre.
bestFor: Budget-minded remote workers settling in for longer, calmer stays
pros: Some of the lowest rents in the city
Everyday shops and services close by
